nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What technology is used for examining highly radioactive samples at Idaho National Laboratory?
nodes.answer: The Idaho National Laboratory uses laboratory-based micro-X-ray computed tomography for examining highly radioactive samples.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What types of examinations are performed during post-irradiation examination (PIE) at INL?
nodes.answer: PIE at INL includes nondestructive techniques like visual inspection and ultrasonics, semi-destructive examinations such as fission-gas sampling, and destructive examinations using methods like focused ion beam (FIB) and scanning electron microscope (SEM).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What techniques are used for the initial examination of irradiated materials at the HFEF?
nodes.answer: The initial examination at the HFEF is performed using nondestructive techniques.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What happens to samples after the initial examination at HFEF?
nodes.answer: After the initial examination, samples can be sectioned into smaller samples to isolate regions of interest and reduce radiation dose rates before being repackaged and sent to specialized examination facilities.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the purpose of using highly shielded containers for irradiated samples?
nodes.answer: The highly shielded containers are used to safely transfer irradiated samples into the facility and minimize radiation exposure to personnel during unloading and preparation.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How are irradiated samples prepared to minimize radiation dose to personnel?
nodes.answer: Irradiated samples are remotely sectioned, polished, prepared, and mounted using manipulators in a shielded sample preparation area to minimize radiation dose to personnel.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the function of the radiological glovebox in the sample preparation process?
nodes.answer: The radiological glovebox is used for decontamination efforts on samples before they are transferred to the laboratory, ensuring safety when handling radioactive materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What doses of gamma irradiation were used in the study?
nodes.answer: The study used varying doses of gamma irradiation, specifically 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250 Gray.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_008
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What doses of gamma irradiation were applied during the experiment?
nodes.answer: The doses applied were 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250 Gray.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Industry, innovation and infrastructure|Industrial safety standards|Radiation safety protocols_qna_009
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How were the control samples treated in comparison to the experimental samples?
nodes.answer: The control samples were not exposed to gamma irradiation, while the experimental samples were subjected to varying doses of irradiation.
